learning_outcomes.text: Capacity to solve problems within their area of study.
Capacity for abstraction: capacity to create and use models that reflect real situations.
Capacity to act autonomously.
Capacity for planning and organizing personal work.
Capacity for effective oral and written communication (in expression and comprehension), with special emphasis on drafting technical documentation.

Understanding and mastery of basic concepts of fields and waves and electromagnetism, electric circuit theory, electronic circuits, physical principle of semiconductors and logic families, electronic and photonic devices, and their application to solving engineering problems.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts of electric circuit theory and its application to solving engineering problems.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts of electronic circuits, physical principle of semiconductors and logic families, and their application to solving engineering problems.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts of electronic and photonic devices and their application to solving engineering problems.
Know the basic elements of a circuit and the equations that govern its operation.
Know and understand the basic laws and theorems for circuit resolution.
Be able to analyze basic electrical circuits.
Know and understand the operation and use of some electrical circuits.
Know the basic semiconductor components used in electronic circuits and their behavior as circuit elements.
Understand the operating principle of basic semiconductor components.
Be able to analyze basic circuits with semiconductor components.
Know some basic application circuits and understand their operation.
Be able to use manufacturer datasheets to obtain information.
Know the basic logic families and their main characteristics.
Understand the operation of basic logic families and interconnection possibilities.
Be able to use basic semiconductor components in some common applications.
Know the main combinational and sequential electronic devices.
Understand the operation of the main combinational and sequential electronic devices.
Know some application circuits of combinational and sequential electronic devices and understand their operation.
Know basic photonic devices.
Understand the operation of basic photonic devices.
Know some application circuits of basic photonic devices and understand their operation.
Be able to use manufacturer datasheets for electronic and photonic devices to obtain information.
Be able to develop applications that use electronic and photonic devices.
Be able to configure and program sequential electronic devices for their correct operation.

syllabus_topics: BLOQUE I. CIRCUITOS ELÉCTRICOS
Theme 1. Electric circuits. Passive components and basic laws
Theme 2. Fundamentals of circuit resolution. Theorems
BLOQUE II. DISPOSITIVOS ELECTRÓNICOS
Theme 3. Electronic components. Diodes and transistors
Theme 4. Optoelectronic components. LEDs, displays and photoreceptors
BLOQUE III. CIRCUITOS ELECTRÓNICOS DIGITALES
Theme 5. Logic families. Electrical characteristics and compatibility. Output types
Theme 6. Combinational electronic circuits. Gates and combinational MSI blocks
Theme 7. Sequential electronic circuits. Sequential MSI blocks and memories.
Theme 8. A/D and D/A converters.
BLOQUE IV. MICROCONTROLADORES
Theme 9. Electronic circuits: microcontrollers
Theme 10. Microcontroller applications.
Laboratory Practice 1. Circuits and equipment handling: power supplies and multimeters
Laboratory Practice 2. Electrical circuits and equipment handling: oscilloscopes and function generator
Laboratory Practice 3. Circuit simulation
Laboratory Practice 4. Construction and testing of diode circuits
Laboratory Practice 5. Construction and testing of bipolar transistor circuits
Laboratory Practice 6. Construction and testing of MOSFET circuits
Laboratory Practice 7. Construction and testing of A/D and D/A converters
Laboratory Practice 8. Construction and testing of combinational circuits and compatibility of logic families
Laboratory Practice 9. Construction and testing of sequential circuits.
Laboratory Practice 10. Microcontrollers. Development system, application development, simulation and debugging.

assessment_methods.method: Theory and classroom practice evaluation (Continuous Assessment Itinerary T1)
Theory and classroom practice evaluation (Final Exam Itinerary T2)
Laboratory practice evaluation (Continuous Assessment Itinerary P1) - Practice evaluation
Laboratory practice evaluation (Continuous Assessment Itinerary P1) - Proficiency test
Laboratory practice evaluation (Practical Exam Itinerary P2)

assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained by weighting the theory and classroom practice exam with 7 points and laboratory practices with 3 points. A minimum of 40% of the maximum grade must be obtained in each part to pass the subject. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of 4 and the weighted grade obtained. If one part is passed in the ordinary February call and the other is not, the grade for the passed part is retained for extraordinary calls within the same academic year. Students must participate in evaluation activities totaling at least 50% of the total grade to be graded, otherwise, they will be marked as 'Not Presented'.
